newsitem.title: USA: Michael Kennedy's wife urges end to babysitter probe.
newsitem.headline: Michael Kennedy's wife urges end to babysitter probe.

text.p: The wife of Michael Kennedy, under investigation for allegedly having an affair with his family's underage babysitter, said on Thursday the probe against her estranged husband should be dropped.

"Now that I have been interviewed by the district attorney's office, I hope that the district attorney will conclude that there is no reason to proceed further with this matter," Victoria Gifford Kennedy said in a statement released by her lawyer.

A Massachusetts prosecutor launched an investigation after the allegations were printed in the Boston Globe newspaper in late April. The prosecutor reportedly has been putting pressure on witnesses to cooperate in the case.

Victoria Gifford Kennedy, the daughter of sportscaster Frank Gifford, told prosecutors on Wednesday she had no knowledge of any sex between her husband and the babysitter while the babysitter was underage, Boston newspapers reported.
"She told them she had no knowledge of any underage sexual relationship until November of 1996," a source familiar with the conversations told the Boston Globe.
By November 1996, the babysitter would have been 18. The age of consent for sexual relations in Massachusetts is 16.
Michael Kennedy, 39, the son of the late Robert Kennedy, and the girl -- now 19 -- allegedly had a relationship that started when she was 14 and ended last fall, the Globe has reported.
The girl -- identified as the daughter of Paul and June Verrochi, past contributers to the campaign of Representative Joseph Kennedy -- Michael's brother, has also reportedly talked to prosecutors.

"This has been an extremely sad and difficult time for me, for my family, and for the Verrochi family," Kennedy's estranged wife said. "I am very hopeful that we will all soon be able to move on with our lives, and that the media will respect our privacy."
A spokeswoman for the district attorney declined to comment on the investigation. "This office will have no comment as we continue our review of this matter," spokeswoman Nina Flaherty told Reuters.
